brief:
Build one lab in which a healthy internal HTTP service cannot be reached by name because the host's stub resolver is misconfigured. The lab DNS server (a static zone for `corp.internal`) must be running and correct; the fault must live only in the client-side resolver configuration (for example a nameserver line pointing at an address with no DNS server, or a wrong port-53 target). Use only `dns.resolver_lab` and the allowed checks.

Requirements:
- Serve the service on a loopback address other than 127.0.0.1 and a non-default port, so the learner has to discover it (e.g. with `ss -ltnp`).
- Use documentation address space (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24) for any bogus address.
- Success checks must include `dns.resolver_answers` for the service name, so that pinning the address in `/etc/hosts` does not pass, plus `dns.http_status` for the service health URL.
- The reference solution must fix only the resolver configuration and must overwrite `/etc/resolv.conf` in place (it is bind-mounted; rename-based edits fail).

The mission must not name the misconfigured file, the bogus address, the working nameserver address or the fix. It may name the service and say the service is reported healthy. Hints go from least to most revealing; no hint may contain the complete fix.
